questions.question: What does gross domestic product measure?
choices: The value of all financial assets owned by citizens
The market value of final goods and services produced within a country during a period
Only wages earned by government employees
Only goods exported to other countries

questions.question: Why does GDP count final goods rather than every intermediate purchase?
choices: To exclude all manufacturing from the economy
To measure only household wealth
To remove all business investment
To avoid counting the same production more than once

questions.question: What is nominal GDP?
choices: GDP measured using current prices
GDP adjusted to remove price changes
GDP per person after all taxes
GDP excluding all government activity

questions.question: What is real GDP?
choices: GDP measured only in current prices
The total value of household savings
GDP adjusted for changes in prices
The value of imports minus exports

questions.question: What is GDP per capita?
choices: GDP divided by the inflation rate
GDP divided by population
Population divided by total exports
Government spending divided by tax revenue

questions.question: Which spending category includes household purchases of goods and services?
choices: Consumption
Investment
Government purchases
Net exports

questions.question: Which calculation gives net exports?
choices: Imports minus exports
Exports plus imports
Consumption minus investment
Exports minus imports

questions.question: Why are purchases of newly produced business equipment counted as investment in GDP?
choices: They are transfers between existing stock owners
They are payments for previously produced goods only
They add to productive capital
They directly measure personal happiness

questions.question: Why is the purchase of an existing company's stock not itself production counted in GDP?
choices: It transfers ownership of a financial asset
It creates a new factory automatically
It is always a government purchase
It counts as a newly produced export

questions.question: Why are government transfer payments not counted as government purchases in GDP?
choices: They are always payments to foreign producers
They are not payments for current goods or services produced
They can never affect household spending
They include no monetary value

questions.question: Why can nominal GDP rise even when output is unchanged?
choices: Population must have fallen
Exports must equal imports
The country must have produced more goods
Prices may rise

questions.question: Why is real GDP more useful for comparing output over time?
choices: It includes every unpaid household activity
It measures income distribution exactly
It separates output changes from price changes
It eliminates all data estimation

questions.question: Why is a used car sale generally excluded from current production in GDP?
choices: The car was produced in an earlier period
Cars are never counted in GDP
Only imported cars are final goods
Every resale is treated as a new export

questions.question: Why can GDP underestimate the value of some useful work?
choices: GDP includes every minute of unpaid caregiving
Much unpaid household work is not measured
Only recreational services are measured
GDP excludes all paid service industries

questions.question: Why is GDP not a complete measure of well-being?
choices: It directly measures every person's satisfaction
It includes no goods or services
It counts only leisure activities
It does not fully show distribution, environmental costs, or quality of life

questions.question: GDP rises from $1 trillion to $1.1 trillion while prices rise 10% and output composition is unchanged. What is the approximate real-output change?
choices: No change
A 10% increase
A 20% increase
A 10% decrease

questions.question: A country's GDP is $600 billion and population is 30 million. What is GDP per capita?
A foreign-owned factory produces goods inside a country. How does that production generally enter the country's GDP?
choices: It is excluded because the owners are foreign
It is included because production occurred within the country
It is counted only in the owners' home country's GDP
It is counted only if no goods are sold locally

questions.question: A bakery buys flour and sells bread to households. Which value should be counted to avoid double counting?
choices: Both the full flour value and full bread value
Only the flour's value
Neither value because food is consumed
The final bread's value rather than adding flour again

questions.question: Two countries have the same GDP but different populations. What additional measure helps compare average output per person?
choices: GDP per capita
Total GDP alone
The number of government departments
The total length of national borders
